decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Location Plan dated 14.08.2026; Existing OS Map and Block Plan CR/23/FP/01 dated 27.10.2025; Proposed OS Map and Block Plan CR/25/FP/01.1 dated 27.10.2025; Existing Floor Plans CR/25/FP/02 dated 27.10.2025; Existing Elevations & Section CR/23/FP/03 Rev B dated 27.10.2025; Proposed Floor Plans CR/25/FP/04 Rev A dated 27.10.2025; Proposed Front, Back, Side Elevations & Section CR/23/FP/05 dated 14.08.2026; Cover Letter dated 13.08.2026, Flood Risk Assessment dated 13.11.2028; Energy Statement. Highway Safety Impact Form.Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

Notwithstanding condition 2, prior to first occupation of the development hereby permitted, Cycle parking, shall be provided within the site in accordance with the following requirements:o Provision of a minimum of three long stay cycle parking spaces, to include one space in the front garden for Flat 2.o in an accessible location: the access route to the long stay store should be a minimum of 1.2m wide to enable the bike to enter the store, should involve no more than 2 doors or gates (excluding the store door) which must also have a minimum opening width of 1.2m;o secured: with a British Standard mortice lock or access fob;o fully enclosed: 4 walls and a roof.Reason: To ensure the provision of accessible, secure, and adequate cycle parking facilities.

The development shall not be occupied until details of the means of enclosure and the site layout for pedestrians and cyclists have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The details shall demonstrate safe, unobstructed and convenient access to both dwellings, the cycle-parking facilities and the refuse and recycling storage area. The approved arrangements shall be installed before first occupation and permanently retained.Reason: To provide a safe, secure and accessible environment, maintain the functionality of the site and protect the visual quality of the frontage.

The refuse and recycling storage hereby approved shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and thereafter maintained unless otherwise in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: In the interests of amenity and the recycling of waste materials in support of the Boroughs waste reduction targets.

The residential units hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the Building Regulations Optional requirement G2 for water consumption of no more than 105 litres or less per head per day (excluding allowance of up to five litres for external water consumption) has been complied with. The measures shall thereafter be permanently retained.Reason: To promote water conservation and efficiency measures in all new developments and where possible in the retrofitting of existing stock in accordance with Policy SI 5 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy CP21 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010).

Notwithstanding the approved plans, the front forecourt of the site shall not be used for the parking of motor vehicles at any time.Reason: To maintain safe and unobstructed pedestrian access, prevent a cramped and cluttered frontage, and protect the character and appearance of the street scene, in accordance with Policies DMD 8, DMD 37 and DMD 47 of the Enfield Development Management Document.

The design and structure of the development shall be of such a standard that it will protect residents within the same building or in adjoining buildings from noise and vibration from the development, so that they are not exposed to noise levels indoors of more than 35 dB LAeq 16 hrs daytime and of more than 30 dB LAeq 8 hrs in bedrooms at night. Inside bedrooms 45 dB L Amax is not to be exceeded more than 15 times per nighttime from sources other than emergency sirens.Reason: To safeguard the residential amenity of future occupants.
